import numpy as np

# USDA outlays data from Treasury Bulletins
# Year: Outlays (in millions of dollars)
data = {
    1990: 46011,  # from 1994 bulletin
    1991: 54119,  # from 1994 bulletin
    1992: 56436,  # from 1994 bulletin
    1993: 63143,  # from 1994 bulletin
    1994: 60812,  # from 1999 bulletin (actual, not estimate)
    1995: 56667,  # from 1999 bulletin
    1996: 54338,  # from 1999 bulletin
    1997: 52558,  # from 1999 bulletin
    1998: 53949,  # from 1999 bulletin
}

# Treat 1990 as year "0" for the time variable
years = np.array(list(data.keys()))
outlays = np.array(list(data.values()))
x = years - 1990  # Convert to 0-based index

print("Data points (x, y):")
for i in range(len(x)):
    print(f"  Year {years[i]} (x={x[i]}): ${outlays[i]} million")

# Calculate linear regression
n = len(x)
x_mean = np.mean(x)
y_mean = np.mean(outlays)

print(f"\nn = {n}")
print(f"x_mean = {x_mean}")
print(f"y_mean = {y_mean}")

# Calculate slope and y-intercept
numerator = np.sum((x - x_mean) * (outlays - y_mean))
denominator = np.sum((x - x_mean) ** 2)

slope = numerator / denominator
y_intercept = y_mean - slope * x_mean

print(f"\nLinear Regression:")
print(f"Slope = {slope}")
print(f"Y-intercept = {y_intercept}")

# Predict for 1999 (x = 9)
x_1999 = 1999 - 1990  # x = 9
predicted_1999 = slope * x_1999 + y_intercept

print(f"\nPrediction for 1999:")
print(f"  x = {x_1999}")
print(f"  Predicted outlays = {predicted_1999}")

# Round as specified
slope_rounded = round(slope, 2)
y_intercept_rounded = round(y_intercept)
predicted_rounded = round(predicted_1999)

print(f"\nFinal answers (rounded):")
print(f"  Slope: {slope_rounded}")
print(f"  Y-intercept: {y_intercept_rounded}")
print(f"  Predicted 1999 outlays: {predicted_rounded}")

print(f"\nAnswer format: [{slope_rounded}, {y_intercept_rounded}, {predicted_rounded}]")
EOF
